source.author: ov
source.text: Quippe ubi temperiem sumpsere umorque calorque, concipiunt, et ab his oriuntur cuncta duobus; cumque sit ignis aquae pugnax, vapor umidus omnes res creat, et discors concordia fetibus apta est.
source.text_original: Quippe ubi temperiem sumpsere umorque calorque, / concipiunt, et ab his oriuntur cuncta duobus; / cumque sit ignis aquae pugnax, vapor umidus omnes / res creat, et discors concordia fetibus apta est.
source.text_english: For when moisture and heat have taken on a balanced blend, they conceive, and from these two all things arise; and although fire is at odds with water, moist vapor creates all things, and this discordant harmony is fit for offspring.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: cumque sit ignis aquae , uapor umidus omnes res creat et discors concordia fetibus apta.
reuse.text_original: cumque sit ignis aquae , uapor umidus omnes res creat et discors concordia fetibus apta.
reuse.text_english: And since fire is the water’s vapor, moist vapor generates all things, and a discordant harmony suited to offspring.
